fruits.extendedStory: Work started in 1226 under the architect Petrus Petri. The style is Gothic, which means height, pointed arches, and as much window as the stone will allow. The cathedral is dedicated to the virgin birth of Jesus. It has been the middle of Christian Toledo for eight centuries. Synagogues and a mosque still stand within a few streets of it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Arbeiten begannen 1226 unter dem Baumeister Petrus Petri. Der Stil ist gotisch, also Höhe, Spitzbögen und so viel Fenster, wie der Stein zulässt. Geweiht ist der Dom der Jungfrauengeburt. Seit acht Jahrhunderten ist er die Mitte des christlichen Toledo. Synagogen und eine Moschee stehen bis heute wenige Gassen entfernt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Work started in 1226 under the architect Petrus Petri. The style is Gothic, which means height, pointed arches, and as much window as the stone will allow. The cathedral is dedicated to the virgin birth of Jesus. It has been the middle of Christian Toledo for eight centuries. Synagogues and a mosque still stand within a few streets of it.

localizedStory.de: Der Baumeister Petrus Petri begann diesen Dom 1226, in der gotischen Weise der Spitzbögen.
localizedStory.en: The architect Petrus Petri began this cathedral in 1226, in the Gothic manner of pointed arches.

fruits.name: Catedral de Santa María
fruits.story: The architect Petrus Petri began this cathedral in 1226, in the Gothic manner of pointed arches.

fruits.extendedStory: Three architects took the old fortress in hand from 1535. They were Alonso de Covarrubias, Francisco de Villalpando and Juan de Herrera. In 1936 it stood through a siege of seventy days and came out almost completely destroyed. What you see is a rebuilding. Inside are the Army Museum and the library of Castile-La Mancha, and the walls rise 60 metres over the town.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Ab 1535 nahmen drei Baumeister die alte Festung in die Hand. Es waren Alonso de Covarrubias, Francisco de Villalpando und Juan de Herrera. 1936 überstand sie eine Belagerung von siebzig Tagen und war danach fast völlig zerstört. Was man sieht, ist ein Wiederaufbau. Drinnen sind das Heeresmuseum und die Bibliothek von Kastilien-La Mancha, und die Mauern ragen 60 Meter über die Stadt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Three architects took the old fortress in hand from 1535. They were Alonso de Covarrubias, Francisco de Villalpando and Juan de Herrera. In 1936 it stood through a siege of seventy days and came out almost completely destroyed. What you see is a rebuilding. Inside are the Army Museum and the library of Castile-La Mancha, and the walls rise 60 metres over the town.

localizedStory.de: Eine Festung, ab 1535 umgebaut, 1936 zerstört und wieder aufgerichtet. Heute steht eine Bibliothek darin.
localizedStory.en: A fortress made over from 1535, wrecked in 1936, and put back up again. A library sits in it now.

fruits.name: Alcázar de Toledo
fruits.story: A fortress made over from 1535, wrecked in 1936, and put back up again. A library sits in it now.

fruits.extendedStory: Juan Guas built this for the Catholic Monarchs, a Franciscan house tied to the crown. It was meant to celebrate victories, to show power and to show devotion, all at once. The oddest part is on the outside. Chains hang along the walls, put there in memory of Christian captives who were set free. Here the history is not just told, it hangs on the wall where you can see it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Juan Guas baute dies für die Katholischen Könige, ein Franziskanerhaus an der Krone. Es sollte Siege feiern, Macht zeigen und Frömmigkeit zeigen, alles zugleich. Das Merkwürdigste hängt außen. An den Mauern hängen Ketten, angebracht zur Erinnerung an befreite christliche Gefangene. Hier wird Geschichte nicht nur erzählt, sie hängt sichtbar an der Wand.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Juan Guas built this for the Catholic Monarchs, a Franciscan house tied to the crown. It was meant to celebrate victories, to show power and to show devotion, all at once. The oddest part is on the outside. Chains hang along the walls, put there in memory of Christian captives who were set free. Here the history is not just told, it hangs on the wall where you can see it.

localizedStory.de: Schau an die Außenmauern. Dort hängen Ketten, zur Erinnerung an befreite Gefangene.
localizedStory.en: Look at the outside walls. Chains hang there, in memory of captives who were set free.

fruits.name: Monasterio de San Juan de los Reyes
fruits.story: Look at the outside walls. Chains hang there, in memory of captives who were set free.

fruits.extendedStory: The tower was a minaret before it was a bell tower. The lord of Orgaz had it rebuilt in the fourteenth century, in brick and masonry. Inside the church hangs the Burial of the Count of Orgaz. El Greco painted it in 1586 for the parish priest Andres Nunez de Toledo. It hangs in the chapel where the count lies, which is why it has never left the building.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Turm war ein Minarett, bevor er Glockenturm wurde. Der Herr von Orgaz ließ ihn im vierzehnten Jahrhundert neu aufmauern, in Ziegel und Bruchstein. In der Kirche hängt das Begräbnis des Grafen von Orgaz. El Greco malte es 1586 für den Pfarrer Andres Nunez de Toledo. Es hängt in der Kapelle, in der der Graf liegt, und darum hat es das Haus nie verlassen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The tower was a minaret before it was a bell tower. The lord of Orgaz had it rebuilt in the fourteenth century, in brick and masonry. Inside the church hangs the Burial of the Count of Orgaz. El Greco painted it in 1586 for the parish priest Andres Nunez de Toledo. It hangs in the chapel where the count lies, which is why it has never left the building.

localizedStory.de: Der Glockenturm war einmal ein Minarett. Drinnen hängt das Bild, das El Greco für genau diese Kapelle malte.
localizedStory.en: The bell tower was a minaret once. Inside hangs the painting El Greco made for this very chapel.

fruits.name: Iglesia de Santo Tomé
fruits.story: The bell tower was a minaret once. Inside hangs the painting El Greco made for this very chapel.

fruits.extendedStory: Samuel ha-Levi was adviser and treasurer to Pedro I of Castile, and he had this synagogue built between 1355 and 1357. The style is Mudéjar, the work of Muslim craftsmen building for Christian and Jewish patrons. Its walls are covered with Hebrew inscriptions that historians have pored over ever since. Since 1964 the building has held the Sephardic Museum. A treasurer's synagogue became a museum of the people who prayed in it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Samuel ha-Levi war Berater und Schatzmeister Pedros I. von Kastilien und ließ diese Synagoge zwischen 1355 und 1357 errichten. Der Stil ist Mudéjar, die Arbeit muslimischer Handwerker für christliche und jüdische Auftraggeber. Die Wände sind mit hebräischen Inschriften bedeckt, über denen Historiker seither brüten. Seit 1964 beherbergt das Haus das Sephardische Museum. Aus der Synagoge eines Schatzmeisters wurde ein Museum derer, die darin beteten.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Samuel ha-Levi was adviser and treasurer to Pedro I of Castile, and he had this synagogue built between 1355 and 1357. The style is Mudéjar, the work of Muslim craftsmen building for Christian and Jewish patrons. Its walls are covered with Hebrew inscriptions that historians have pored over ever since. Since 1964 the building has held the Sephardic Museum. A treasurer's synagogue became a museum of the people who prayed in it.

localizedStory.de: Der Schatzmeister des Königs ließ diese Synagoge zwischen 1355 und 1357 bauen. Hebräische Schrift bedeckt die Wände.
localizedStory.en: The king's treasurer had this synagogue built between 1355 and 1357. Hebrew writing covers its walls.

fruits.name: Sinagoga del Tránsito
fruits.story: The king's treasurer had this synagogue built between 1355 and 1357. Hebrew writing covers its walls.

fruits.extendedStory: The building went up in 1180 as a synagogue. Its architecture is Moorish, the manner of the Islamic craftsmen who worked in Spain, with horseshoe arches and white plaster. Later it took a Christian name, Virgen Blanca, the White Virgin. One building, three faiths in its history, and it is still standing.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Bau entstand 1180 als Synagoge. Die Architektur ist maurisch, die Art der islamischen Handwerker in Spanien, mit Hufeisenbögen und weißem Putz. Später bekam er einen christlichen Namen, Virgen Blanca, die Weiße Jungfrau. Ein Gebäude, drei Glauben in seiner Geschichte, und es steht noch.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The building went up in 1180 as a synagogue. Its architecture is Moorish, the manner of the Islamic craftsmen who worked in Spain, with horseshoe arches and white plaster. Later it took a Christian name, Virgen Blanca, the White Virgin. One building, three faiths in its history, and it is still standing.

localizedStory.de: 1180 als Synagoge erbaut, in maurischer Bauweise, und später christlich benannt.
localizedStory.en: Built as a synagogue in 1180, in the Moorish manner, and later given a Christian name.

fruits.name: Sinagoga de Santa María la Blanca
fruits.story: Built as a synagogue in 1180, in the Moorish manner, and later given a Christian name.

fruits.extendedStory: This was an oratory before it was a church, built beside a gate called Bab al-Mardum, which gave it its name. Inside are nine bays under ribbed vaults and horseshoe arches. The four middle columns wear Visigothic capitals, carved long before and reused here. The story goes that Alfonso VI's horse stopped and bowed on this spot. A crucifix was found where it stood, with a lamp beside it still burning after centuries.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Dies war ein Gebetsraum, bevor es eine Kirche wurde, gebaut neben einem Tor namens Bab al-Mardum, das ihm den Namen gab. Drinnen sind neun Joche unter Rippengewölben und Hufeisenbögen. Die vier mittleren Säulen tragen westgotische Kapitelle, lange vorher gehauen und hier wiederverwendet. Die Geschichte will, dass Alfonsos VI. Pferd hier stehen blieb und sich verneigte. Wo es stand, fand man ein Kruzifix, daneben eine Lampe, die nach Jahrhunderten noch brannte.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This was an oratory before it was a church, built beside a gate called Bab al-Mardum, which gave it its name. Inside are nine bays under ribbed vaults and horseshoe arches. The four middle columns wear Visigothic capitals, carved long before and reused here. The story goes that Alfonso VI's horse stopped and bowed on this spot. A crucifix was found where it stood, with a lamp beside it still burning after centuries.

localizedStory.de: Neun kleine Joche, Hufeisenbögen und vier Säulen, deren Kapitelle schon alt waren, als man sie wiederverwendete.
localizedStory.en: Nine little bays, horseshoe arches, and four columns whose tops were old already when they were reused.

fruits.name: Mezquita del Cristo de la Luz
fruits.story: Nine little bays, horseshoe arches, and four columns whose tops were old already when they were reused.

fruits.extendedStory: People used to call this the gossip-shop of Castile, and that is a fair description. Its name twists an Arabic phrase for the place where pack animals changed hands. Enrique IV granted the weekly fair in 1465. After that, little shops crowded in around the edges, and festivals took the whole square over whenever there was something worth celebrating.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Zocodover ist die spanische Verdrehung eines arabischen Ausdrucks für Markt der Lasttiere, und genau das war er. 1465 gab Enrique IV. Toledo das Recht, hier wöchentlich Markt zu halten. Der Platz füllte sich mit einem Gewimmel kleiner Läden und mit Festen. Man nannte ihn die Schwatzbude Kastiliens, was verrät, was hier wirklich lief.
localizedExtendedStory.en: People used to call this the gossip-shop of Castile, and that is a fair description. Its name twists an Arabic phrase for the place where pack animals changed hands. Enrique IV granted the weekly fair in 1465. After that, little shops crowded in around the edges, and festivals took the whole square over whenever there was something worth celebrating.

localizedStory.de: Der Name kommt aus dem Arabischen und heißt Markt der Lasttiere. Hier wurde Vieh verkauft, lange bevor man sich hier traf.
localizedStory.en: Enrique IV granted Toledo a weekly fair on this ground in 1465. It has been busy ever since.

fruits.name: Plaza de Zocodover
fruits.story: Enrique IV granted Toledo a weekly fair on this ground in 1465. It has been busy ever since.

fruits.extendedStory: A church stood here from 1187 and was pulled down in 1959. The tower is all that survived, and its foundations reach back to a minaret. Look at the openings. They are pointed horseshoe shapes set in a shallow frame called an alfiz, an Almohad habit that is uncommon in Toledo. The building was made over from the middle of the thirteenth century, and this tower is what is left of it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Ab 1187 stand hier eine Kirche, 1959 wurde sie abgerissen. Nur der Turm blieb, und seine Fundamente reichen bis zu einem Minarett zurück. Schau dir die Öffnungen an. Es sind spitze Hufeisenformen in einem flachen Rahmen, einem Alfiz, eine almohadische Gewohnheit, die in Toledo selten ist. Ab der Mitte des dreizehnten Jahrhunderts wurde umgebaut, und dieser Turm ist der Rest davon.
localizedExtendedStory.en: A church stood here from 1187 and was pulled down in 1959. The tower is all that survived, and its foundations reach back to a minaret. Look at the openings. They are pointed horseshoe shapes set in a shallow frame called an alfiz, an Almohad habit that is uncommon in Toledo. The building was made over from the middle of the thirteenth century, and this tower is what is left of it.

localizedStory.de: Die Kirche, die hier stand, fiel 1959. Nur ihr Turm blieb, und der begann als Minarett.
localizedStory.en: The church that stood here came down in 1959. Its tower is all that is left, and it began as a minaret.

fruits.name: Torre de San Cristóbal
fruits.story: The church that stood here came down in 1959. Its tower is all that is left, and it began as a minaret.

fruits.extendedStory: A square usually takes its name from whatever stands on it, and this one is no different. What is worth going inside for is the ceiling of the Corpus Christi chapel. It is wood, painted, and set with glazed tile. Look along the band that runs round its edge. Riders follow one another the whole way: one Christian, then one Muslim, then Christian again.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Platz trägt den Namen der Kirche an ihm, einer der Pfarreien, die Alfonso VI. 1085 nach der Einnahme der Stadt gründete. Die Kirche bewahrt eine Backsteinapsis mit Blendbögen. Ihre Fronleichnamskapelle hat eine bemalte Holzdecke, reich an Fliesenwerk. Um diese Decke läuft ein Fries. Ein christlicher und ein muslimischer Reiter folgen einander rundherum.
localizedExtendedStory.en: A square usually takes its name from whatever stands on it, and this one is no different. What is worth going inside for is the ceiling of the Corpus Christi chapel. It is wood, painted, and set with glazed tile. Look along the band that runs round its edge. Riders follow one another the whole way: one Christian, then one Muslim, then Christian again.

localizedStory.de: In der Kapelle zeigt eine bemalte Decke abwechselnd einen christlichen und einen muslimischen Reiter.
localizedStory.en: In the chapel here a painted ceiling shows a Christian rider and a Muslim rider, turn and turn about.

fruits.name: Plaza de San Justo
fruits.story: In the chapel here a painted ceiling shows a Christian rider and a Muslim rider, turn and turn about.
